4. While the petitioners have been serving under the Corporation, on every occasion advertisements for appointment were published and in those advertisements the employees appointed under the Master Roll were given scope for making application and accordingly the employees who were working under Master Roll made application and they were appointed by the Corporation in the original set up of the Corporation and in 2003 3(three) advertisements were made and published on 06.07.2006, 05.07.2006 and 11.07.2006 and in those advertisements the Corporation kept opinion under Clauses 13 and 14 for the employees working under the Master Roll to make application and in response to those application some of the incumbents were appointed in the posts of Peon and Darwan from Master Roll. Even in almost all organizations including the office of the Hon'ble Prime Minister also gives similar scope in the advertisements. 

 6. While the petitioners have been waiting for being regularized in the original manpower set up of the Corporation, the Corporation instead of absorbing/regularizing the service of the petitioners made advertisement for appointment on 20.06.2013 and the same has been published in the daily Ittefaq on 23.06.2013 and in the said advertisement the respondents authority have not provided any provision/scope for the employees working under the Master Roll/Daily Basis to make any application in total deviation from all the previous advertisements wherein those scope were available for the Master Roll/Daily Basis Employees. 

 7. It is stated that in similar situation and in similar matter some other employees working on Master Roll/Daily Basis moved this Court in Writ Petition No.4301 of 2010 and 8080 of 2009 and in those writ petitions the High Court Division by a judgment and order dated 11.04.2012 made the Rule absolute with a direction to absorb those writ petitioners in the regular manpower set up of the Corporation. 

 8. During the last 30 years, the Corporation have been calling advertisement for appointment giving opportunity for application for being appointed as existing employees and meanwhile 100 employees have been appointed from amongst the employees worked under Master Roll/Daily Basis, the petitioners should not be discriminated in respect of their opportunity for being appointed standing on the same status hence the advertisement for appointment is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and the respondents may be directed to absorb/regularize the petitioners in the original manpower set up of the Corporation. 

 9. Since more recently in 2006 the Corporation recruited employees from Master Roll/Daily Basis in pursuance of the advertisement, the curtailment of the facility has caused serious discrimination to the petitioners and therefore, the advertisement for appointment is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and the respondents may be directed to absorb/regularize the petitioners in the original manpower set up of the Corporation. 

 10. Since in Writ Petition No.4301 of 2010 and 8080 of 2009 the employees working under Master Roll moved this Court and the Rules have been made absolute with a direction for absorption/regularization, the petitioners are praying for similar relief and therefore, the advertisement for appointment is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and the respondents may be directed to absorb/regularize the petitioners in the original manpower set up of the Corporation. 

 12. The learned Advocate for the petitioners further submits that since more recently in 2006 the Corporation recruited employees from Master Roll/Daily Basis in pursuance of the advertisement, the curtailment of the facility has caused serious discrimination to the petitioners and therefore, the advertisement for appointment is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and the respondents may be directed to absorb/regularize the petitioners in the original manpower set up of the Corporation. 

 13. The learned Advocate for the petitioners next submits that since in Writ Petition No.4301 of 2010 and 8080 of 2009 the employees working under Master Roll moved this Court and the Rules have been made absolute with a direction for absorption/regularization, the petitioners are praying for similar relief and therefore, the advertisement for appointment is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and the respondents may be directed to absorb/regularize the petitioners in the original manpower set up of the Corporation. 

 15. He further submits that the contents of this writ petition is that as per service regulations of BADC, 1990 the authority decided to appoint some Employees in direct process and Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) published advertisement in the daily news papers namely the Daily Ittefaq and the Daily Jonokantha for appointment/fulfill of 201 post Peon and Darwan/Guard 230 post, vide their office order Memo No.12.204.011.05.04.148.2013-626 dated 23.06.2013 as per advertisement the require qualification was class Eight pass. The age limit of the applicant was 30 years and 32 years for freedom fighter kotha. Which was as per provision of service regulations of BADC of 1990 in that advertisement the authority could not mention any provision/scope for absorption/ regularization of the employees working under the Master Roll/Daily Basis by following the provision of the service regulations of BADC of 1990, as per provision of service regulation of BADC of 1990 there have no scope of absorption/ regularization of the employees working under the Master Roll/Daily Basis, provision of that regulations is direct recruitment. 

 16. The learned DAG appearing for the respondents next submits that the petitioners of Writ Petition No.4301 of 2010 and 8080 of 2009 were working under Master Roll and Daily Basis worker of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) in different post and place in. Bangladesh and they have been applied for of those posts for direct recruitment, but in this case the petitioners also were working under Master Roll and Daily Basis worker of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) in different post and place in Bangladesh, but they did not submit any application without doing this they are demanding their absorption/regularization, which is beyond the service regulations of BADC, 1990. 

 17. The learned DAG appearing for the respondents lastly submits that in the meantime some employees of this writ petition who is working as Master Roll and Daily Basis worker under Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) in different post and place in Bangladesh and they engaged themselves with corruption, specially the petitioner No.25 of this Writ Petition namely Md. Belal Hossain who is working under the Corporation at Rangpur office as daily basis Darwan, BADC seeds Dealer Association, Rangpur raise written objection before BADC authority against Md. Belal Hossain stating that he is carrying business and selling lower grade Potato seeds, collecting from different District of Rangpur and Dinajpur Zone. Receiving that objection BADC authority formed enquiry committee, they enquired the matter and found reality against Md. Belal Hossain and submitted enquiry report against him. 

 20. It appears from the record that the petitioners were engaged by the BADC authority at various dates as Peon, Darwan/Guard under Master Roll/Daily Basis. The respondent No.4 published an advertisement on 20.06.2013 in the daily Ittefaq for appointment of Bangladeshi Nationals for several posts. The petitioners applied for the said post. We note that after completion of all formalities starting from issuing interview cards, taking viva voce examination and practical tests, the respondents all on a sudden stayed the results and published yet another fresh circular against the said post. It is the right of the petitioners to know the results of the interview and the practical examinations. In the instant case the respondents without publishing the results of the said examination went on with the process of re-advertisement. Further more we note that the authority concern categorically mentioned that those persons who are already working on a Master Roll/Daily Basis are to get priority. 

 21. It is to be noted that the Member Director (Seed and Garden) of BADC wrote a letter on 09.12.2002 and requested the project Director to regularize the employees who have been working on master roll basis. The said letter has created a legitimate expectation in the minds of the petitioners. Extract of the said letter runs as follows: 

 22. The doctrine of legitimate expectation is only an aspect which does not give rise to an enforceable right but only provides that the action taken by the authority while dealing with the citizens is not arbitrary. The doctrine of legitimate expectation must yield whenever required, to larger public interest in appropriate cases. An examination of the aforenoted letter aroused an expectation in the minds of the petitioners that they will be absorbed at some point in time. Furthermore we can not lost sight of the fact that the respondents without publishing the results of the examination in which the petitioners had appeared went on with the process of re-advertisement. It is also pertinent to mention here that the authority concern categorically mentioned that those persons who are already working on Master Roll/Daily Basis are to get priority.
